scope: All control records in the current synthetic DOM inventory; includes repeated instances and hidden legacy controls, not simultaneously visible controls.

decisions.title: Colour mode
decisions.alternative: Light / Dark / Automatic in one segmented choice. Selecting a mode immediately updates a nearby live preview; Automatic has a short sunrise/sunset explanation.
decisions.reason: Three mutually exclusive values should be discoverable without opening a menu. A binary switch cannot faithfully express three modes.

decisions.title: Six palette choices
decisions.alternative: Six labeled visual tiles using the selected mode’s actual surfaces, text and accents. A check marks the chosen palette.
decisions.reason: A visual choice already uses a visual interaction. Improve fidelity rather than invent a new control.

decisions.title: Text size
decisions.alternative: Standard / Larger as visible choices beside real examples of labels, calendar events and widget text. Apply immediately.
decisions.reason: Two values do not warrant a hidden menu. The sample should demonstrate legibility rather than decorative placeholder content.

decisions.title: Starting layout
decisions.alternative: Small previews of Balanced, Photos first and Agenda first. Open them through “Choose a layout”; selecting one previews replacement before Apply. Custom is a current-state label, not a disabled option.
decisions.reason: The choice is spatial. A name alone does not show what will move or disappear. Replacement needs explicit scope and a Cancel route.

decisions.title: Arrange neatly
decisions.alternative: Remove this button. Offer the visual layout templates for intentional replacement. When a widget cannot fit, explain the constraint and let the owner make room.
decisions.reason: The current action repacks everything into equal-size tiles. “Neatly” hides a substantial and potentially unwanted reset.

decisions.title: Undo and Redo
decisions.alternative: Remove the permanent pair from the toolbar. After a meaningful move/remove/replacement, offer a quiet Undo action while the draft exists. Keep keyboard history available; Cancel restores the saved layout.
decisions.reason: Recovery remains important, but two permanently visible editing commands do not need equal weight with composition. Do not make the only recovery route a short-lived toast.

decisions.title: Preview screen
decisions.alternative: Match the current dashboard’s viewport and aspect ratio automatically. Scale that exact canvas to the available editor space. Put alternate-size checks in developer tooling.
decisions.reason: Screen geometry is known. Asking the owner to choose a testing resolution exposes our development workflow.

decisions.title: Expand canvas
decisions.alternative: Remove the button. Open arrangement in a sufficiently spacious workspace, adapting palette and inspector into temporary panels when necessary.
decisions.reason: A user should not have to repair the editor’s allocation of space. Current expansion hides tools without meaningfully enlarging the captured canvas.

decisions.title: Widget palette: add and drag
decisions.alternative: One recognizable card per widget with an integrated drag affordance. Tap places it in a suitable free spot; drag shows the destination before release. Already-added cards show a clear state.
decisions.reason: Two separate button identities for each widget should not become two visually competing operations. Preserve tap and keyboard alternatives to dragging.

decisions.title: Move and resize affordances
decisions.alternative: Drag a widget body to move it; use a modest corner grip to resize. Enlarge invisible hit areas instead of drawing huge handles. Show snapping and invalid placement directly on the canvas.
decisions.reason: The object is the best control. Keep focused keyboard movement and resizing with concise help in an accessible support route.

decisions.title: Column, Row, Width and Height
decisions.alternative: Remove all four. Drag/resize with snapping; optionally offer useful named sizes as a shortcut. Keep keyboard equivalents.
decisions.reason: These are layout-engine coordinates, not owner preferences. Hiding them in Advanced would retain the wrong model.

decisions.title: Clock style
decisions.alternative: Landscape, Analog, Flip and Botanical thumbnails using the selected widget’s current proportions and theme. Selecting one changes the widget in place.
decisions.reason: The owner chooses an appearance. The live widget supplies the preview; a second expandable clock sample is redundant.

decisions.title: Remove module
decisions.alternative: Show a recognizable Remove action only for the selected widget, with an accessible text label and recovery in the draft.
decisions.reason: Removal belongs to selection. It must not compete with every widget or require searching a general inspector form.

decisions.title: Save dashboard and Discard changes
decisions.alternative: Stable Apply and Cancel controls. Apply appears enabled when the draft differs; Cancel abandons the draft. Leaving with a draft must offer an explicit outcome.
decisions.reason: Spatial editing benefits from experimentation. Clear draft boundaries solve this without turning the whole Settings area into a form.

decisions.title: Today’s accessory / automatic variation
decisions.alternative: An “Change accessories automatically” switch controls variation. When on, show Daily / Frequent as cadence choices, with the actual interval explained. When off, select a fixed accessory in the gallery.
decisions.reason: Automatic variation is a policy; a hat is an object. Mixing both in one list hides the distinction. Preserve existing cadence on migration rather than silently choosing a new one.

decisions.title: Accessory gallery
decisions.alternative: One gallery with live Momo thumbnails, including None. Tap a tile to wear it immediately; mark selection. In automatic mode, preview a hat without silently changing the policy.
decisions.reason: This is the human-friendly interaction already present. Remove the duplicate text list and make the mode relationship explicit.

decisions.title: His energy
decisions.alternative: Playful / Gentle / Still with tiny illustrative motion previews. Selecting one updates Momo; respect reduced-motion preferences.
decisions.reason: Three named behaviors deserve a visible, comparable choice, not an obscured dropdown.

decisions.title: His daily rhythm
decisions.alternative: A clearly labeled “Rest at night” switch with the effective hours shown and a link to Daily routine. Allow an intentional independent rhythm where needed.
decisions.reason: This is a binary policy. The relationship to the frame’s other night behavior should be explained, not inferred.

decisions.title: Try another accessory
decisions.alternative: A small shuffle icon with an accessible “Try another” label beside the preview. In fixed mode it chooses a new fixed accessory; in automatic mode it previews the next one without disabling automatic variation.
decisions.reason: An action needs a predictable effect. It is distinct from turning ongoing variation on.

decisions.title: Make a face
decisions.alternative: A small clearly named interaction beside Momo, secondary to the preference controls. Respect Still/reduced motion and avoid making it a large configuration action.
decisions.reason: It adds delight and helps demonstrate behavior; it does not need form-level emphasis.

decisions.title: Find your city and Find
decisions.alternative: Start with the selected city and a Change action. Search opens a labeled query field with result rows; choose a result to commit, or Cancel. Keep submit available for keyboard users.
decisions.reason: Configured state and pending search are different states. Do not leave owners guessing which city is active.

decisions.title: Temperature
decisions.alternative: °C / °F as labeled mutually exclusive choices. Update weather examples immediately.
decisions.reason: A two-option enum should be visible. Retain names for accessibility rather than relying on symbols alone.

decisions.title: Clock format
decisions.alternative: 12-hour / 24-hour with a live time example. One shared preference for all clocks and schedule displays.
decisions.reason: The choice is small and its effect easy to demonstrate. It should not be repeated on every widget.

decisions.title: Photo source
decisions.alternative: Show the selected source and its verified status. “Change source” opens two labeled source cards, each explaining what it supports. Connection fields appear only in the appropriate flow.
decisions.reason: A source determines capabilities, not just a value in a menu. Switching should not silently disconnect or erase the inactive source.

decisions.title: Slideshow style and duplicate style previews
decisions.alternative: Five labeled style tiles with brief representative motion: fade, prints, collage, pan/zoom and still. A single selector owns the value. Preview motion on selection, respecting reduced motion.
decisions.reason: “Soft fade” alone requires prior knowledge. Existing three preview buttons duplicate the dropdown and omit two styles.

decisions.title: Seconds per picture
decisions.alternative: A compact pace selector, for example Quick · 8s / Relaxed · 20s / Lingering · 1 min, plus a deliberate More durations sheet for existing longer options. Show the exact applied duration.
decisions.reason: Few useful defaults reduce scanning without removing supported long durations. Existing nonpreset values remain visible as Custom, never silently rounded.

decisions.title: Play collection
decisions.alternative: A row showing the current collection and count opens a thumbnail list of collections, including Recent, Keepers, Favourites and memories. Empty collections show their state.
decisions.reason: An unbounded/custom collection set justifies a picker; it should show what will play rather than present only names.

decisions.title: Preview presentation
decisions.alternative: One clearly named “Preview slideshow” beside style/pace choices. Opens the actual chosen collection and settings, then returns to the same location.
decisions.reason: Preview is useful for motion. It must communicate whether it previews manual playback or automatic display, rather than ambiguously saying presentation.

decisions.title: Automatic mail check
decisions.alternative: Under Receiving, show Every 15 min / Hourly / Daily with the next check or manual Check now nearby. Keep the three existing options.
decisions.reason: This is a small policy set, not a technical text field. Delivery state helps the owner judge the choice.

decisions.title: Trusted senders and address entry
decisions.alternative: “Only accept photos from these people” switch; when on, show sender rows with Add/Remove and a focused email entry. Allow bulk paste as an optional shortcut.
decisions.reason: One-address-per-line text is an implementation convenience. Exact-address matching still matters; empty-list behavior must be explicit before enabling restriction.

controls.label: Exact email addresses · one per line

decisions.title: Save delivery options
decisions.alternative: Ordinary delivery choices apply when valid. A sender Add flow commits an address explicitly and can be canceled. Show nearby validation/save failure.
decisions.reason: A separate Save button gives this preference group a different persistence model without explaining why.

decisions.title: Gmail address, app password and Connect
decisions.alternative: A focused account connection flow with labeled email/password fields, show/hide password while editing, clear prerequisites and Connect. Use a real imported photo to verify success.
decisions.reason: Credentials genuinely require entry. Simplification must not become a fake one-click sign-in, prefilled secret or unverifiable “connected” state.

decisions.title: Gallery retention
decisions.alternative: Visible recommended choices Last 30 days / Last 90 days / Last 30 photos; More opens all existing choices grouped by age or count. Summarize the effective rule and impact before pruning.
decisions.reason: Age and count are different policies. A structured picker shows that distinction; a dropdown of eleven interleaved-looking values does not explain retention.

decisions.title: Maximum shown photos
decisions.alternative: Use the existing bounded capacity automatically for new setups. If an owner has a custom additional cap, show it explicitly on the retention detail page as “Also limit recent photos to …”.
decisions.reason: A second unlabeled constraint can contradict the chosen policy. Preserve existing caps unless the owner deliberately changes them; never erase a migration choice silently.

decisions.title: Disconnect email / erase local cache
decisions.alternative: Separate source detail “Disconnect and erase local photos” from storage detail “Clear local photos.” Show exact scope in confirmation and a clear Cancel; do not alter the mailbox.
decisions.reason: Similar verbs have different outcomes. These actions need deliberate context and remain immediately available for revocation.

controls.label: Disconnect email and erase saved pictures

decisions.title: Composition
decisions.alternative: Three illustrated tiles: Automatic, One picture, Two pictures. Automatic explains portrait pairing; selected style previews the effective layout.
decisions.reason: Arrangement is spatial. A text dropdown conceals the strongest distinction.

decisions.title: Default framing
decisions.alternative: Fit / Fill / Automatic over one sample photo, showing preserved edges versus cropping. Automatic briefly explains its decision.
decisions.reason: Seeing the crop is more meaningful than learning the words. Keep the global default separate from a picture override.

decisions.title: Surrounding space
decisions.alternative: Theme mat / Black / Picture background tiles around the same sample image. Preview the current theme’s actual mat.
decisions.reason: This is another appearance choice with a readily visible effect; do not make the owner translate text into visuals.

decisions.title: Transition duration
decisions.alternative: A small speed choice beside a selected transition, with a preview replay action. “None” is represented by Cut rather than a contradictory independent duration value.
decisions.reason: Transition type and timing must form a coherent result. Preserve legitimate saved timing while showing the actual effective combination.

decisions.title: Transition type
decisions.alternative: Polished defaults come from the style. If customization is requested, show animated Dissolve / Cut / Slide / Reveal / Variety tiles on a motion page.
decisions.reason: The style and transition menus overlap. A dedicated visual customization page is earned only by an intentional customization task.

decisions.title: Browsing playback seconds
decisions.alternative: Default browsing playback to the chosen pace. Preserve an existing separate value as an explicit “Browsing pace differs” row with a duration picker if this distinction remains supported.
decisions.reason: A second number with unclear playback scope is fiddly. Unification should be intentional and preserve established preferences.

decisions.title: Allow gentle motion
decisions.alternative: “Motion in slideshow” switch beside the motion preview; show Still when reduced motion takes precedence. Do not allow a toggle that falsely promises an unavailable effect.
decisions.reason: A binary accessibility-sensitive behavior needs observable state and clear precedence.

decisions.title: Resume previous photo
decisions.alternative: “Continue where I left off” under playback behavior, with a short explanation of which automatic/manual sessions it applies to.
decisions.reason: This is a valid preference with a clear human consequence; the existing wording and scope need refinement.

decisions.title: Legacy Shuffle and Favourites-only
decisions.alternative: Keep one Photo order choice and one collection picker. Migrate legacy flags into those canonical settings.
decisions.reason: These hidden legacy controls duplicate current choices. They need retirement/migration, not new visual styling.

decisions.title: Repeat slideshow
decisions.alternative: Repeat / Play once when starting a deliberate presentation. Ambient photo display loops by design; existing finite-playback settings remain honored in the appropriate mode.
decisions.reason: A wall frame and a one-off presentation have different purposes. Do not force the owner to configure a routine slideshow’s basic continuity.

decisions.title: Prefer favourites on Overview
decisions.alternative: In the selected Photos widget, show its collection preference with a direct Favourites choice. Link to the library for starring photos.
decisions.reason: This affects one dashboard widget, not slideshow order. Place it beside the surface it changes.

decisions.title: Photo order
decisions.alternative: Newest / Oldest / Shuffle / My order. Choosing My order opens the sequence editor; only that mode exposes sequence-management tools.
decisions.reason: Four exclusive modes can be visible. Their differing interactions should be conditional, not laid out simultaneously.

decisions.title: Queue new arrivals next
decisions.alternative: Show “Show new photos sooner” when the chosen order supports it, with a plain explanation that current playback is not interrupted.
decisions.reason: This policy is separate from sorting. Its effective behavior should not require understanding an internal queue.

decisions.title: Give favourites extra turns
decisions.alternative: Under Shuffle, offer “Show favourites more often” with a clear on/off choice and a preview/brief explanation.
decisions.reason: Weighting is meaningful only in the relevant playback modes. Avoid implying it changes chronological or manual order.

decisions.title: Sequence drag/up/down controls
decisions.alternative: Reorder thumbnail tiles by drag; offer accessible Move earlier/later actions for the focused item through a contextual menu. Clear Done/Cancel applies the sequence.
decisions.reason: Each photo currently carries three controls. The same functionality can be available without three permanent buttons per row.

decisions.title: Find a picture
decisions.alternative: A compact search field above the gallery with clear/reset, relevant result count and an empty-result state.
decisions.reason: Search is justified when the library grows. It belongs where pictures are visible, rather than halfway through preferences.

decisions.title: Show / library filter
decisions.alternative: Visible primary collections/filters in the library; less common Excluded and Waiting for review appear as labeled destinations, with pending counts. Collapse to a picker on smaller screens.
decisions.reason: Seven states mix collections, dates and moderation. Grouping helps people understand where they are.

decisions.title: Select all matching / Clear selection
decisions.alternative: Enter Select mode first. Only then show Select all results and Deselect all, with an explicit count and search scope.
decisions.reason: Selection commands make little sense before selection is an active task. “All” must state whether it means displayed results or the entire library.

decisions.title: Per-photo checkboxes
decisions.alternative: Normal mode: tap a photo to inspect. Select mode: tap toggles a clear selection check overlay on the image. Provide an accessible Select action; do not depend only on long press.
decisions.reason: Permanent checkboxes make every photo card look like a form before the person chooses a bulk task.

decisions.title: Repeated Edit buttons
decisions.alternative: Tap the photo to open its viewer; Edit opens the framing/details tool from there. Keyboard activation follows the same route.
decisions.reason: Every item does not need a labeled Edit button and a checkbox below its image. Mode separation makes the interaction legible.

decisions.title: Keep / Remove from Keepers
decisions.alternative: Show Keep for unprotected selection and Stop keeping for protected selection. Mixed selection states are explicit. Explain retention protection once in that workflow.
decisions.reason: Opposite actions should not appear equally available without regard to selection. Keepers is not simply another collection.

decisions.title: Favourite
decisions.alternative: An accessible star in the viewer and selection toolbar. Indicate on/off/mixed state; batch action states the intended outcome.
decisions.reason: Starring is a lightweight preference. A bare Favourite verb hides whether it adds, removes or toggles a mixed selection.

decisions.title: Exclude / Restore
decisions.alternative: Exclude appears for eligible photos; Restore appears in Excluded. Confirm the persistent exclusion effect, show an Undo route, and preserve exclusions across mail checks.
decisions.reason: Opposite actions do not need to sit beside each other at all times. Deletion from email must not be implied.

decisions.title: New collection and Create with selected
decisions.alternative: With photos selected, “Add to collection” offers Existing or New. New opens a name field with Create/Cancel and a count of included photos.
decisions.reason: Naming and bulk membership are one task. Empty name fields should not occupy the default gallery.

decisions.title: Existing collection picker / add / remove
decisions.alternative: Add selected opens a collection picker. Remove from collection is offered only inside a particular collection and never erases photos.
decisions.reason: The operation needs a known collection context. A global remove button and empty dropdown require guesswork.

decisions.title: Delete collection
decisions.alternative: Put Delete collection in that collection’s menu. Confirm that pictures stay on the frame, with Cancel.
decisions.reason: A destructive action against a container should not be mixed into photo-selection controls.

decisions.title: Picture selector
decisions.alternative: The picture opened in the viewer is the editing target. Previous/Next moves through the current library scope with unsaved-edit handling.
decisions.reason: A separate text dropdown disconnects editing from the selected image and duplicates gallery navigation.

decisions.title: Per-photo Favourite / Exclude
decisions.alternative: Use the same star and Exclude actions as the library, operating on this photo. Do not provide a second checkbox-based exclusion model inside framing.
decisions.reason: Repeated entry points are fine when they share semantics; duplicate presentations with different state language are confusing.

decisions.title: Picture framing override
decisions.alternative: Default / Fit / Fill choices directly beside the image. Default shows the current inherited behavior and a reset route.
decisions.reason: People need to see both the crop and whether their change affects this photo or every photo.

decisions.title: Caption, title and accessibility description
decisions.alternative: Keep a concise title for finding the photo and an accessibility description in Photo details. Consolidate redundant caption/title roles; keep captions off the player.
decisions.reason: These are metadata, not mandatory slideshow setup. Accessibility description must remain available even if visible captions are omitted.

decisions.title: Rotation
decisions.alternative: Rotate clockwise from the image toolbar, with orientation visible and Reset available. An accessible menu may expose exact orientations.
decisions.reason: Rotation is best understood as an action on the picture, not selecting a degree value from a form.

decisions.title: Capture date
decisions.alternative: A labeled date picker in Photo details, with Unknown/clear state and a brief note explaining its use for memories.
decisions.reason: A date genuinely requires a date control. Never silently infer capture date from received date.

decisions.title: Crop horizontal and vertical
decisions.alternative: In Fill mode, drag the image within a fixed frame; keep edges visible, constrain movement and provide keyboard nudge alternatives.
decisions.reason: Two independent sliders are a poor proxy for a two-dimensional visual task. Fit mode should not expose controls with no effect.

decisions.title: Suggested face position
decisions.alternative: “Suggest framing” previews a local proposal that can be accepted or adjusted. Explain that it uses on-device detection and does not identify people.
decisions.reason: A hidden automatic override and a manual crop can conflict. An explicit suggestion with visible effect is easier to trust.

decisions.title: Custom viewing time
decisions.alternative: A row reads “Use slideshow pace” or the specific duration. A picker offers a small set plus Custom duration, with Reset to slideshow.
decisions.reason: Zero-as-default is a storage encoding. A custom override should express inheritance clearly and require deliberate use.

decisions.title: Save picture details
decisions.alternative: Done/Cancel on the image-editing tool. Preview changes in the draft; warn about a dirty draft before changing the target photo.
decisions.reason: A larger multi-step edit needs a boundary, unlike a quick favourite toggle.

decisions.title: Show excluded / Restore all excluded
decisions.alternative: Use the existing Excluded library destination instead of a second show-hidden flag. Offer Restore all only there, with a clear count and confirmation.
decisions.reason: The destination already provides discovery. A global restore action can reverse many intentional exclusions unexpectedly.

controls.label: Show excluded pictures in the library

decisions.title: Review new emailed pictures
decisions.alternative: “Review photos before showing them” with a pending queue link when enabled and nonempty. Explain what happens to already pending photos when turning it off.
decisions.reason: This controls admission, not storage. It belongs with sender restrictions rather than an arbitrary library accordion.

controls.label: Review new emailed pictures before display

decisions.title: Keep capture date from new imports
decisions.alternative: A clear “Remember capture dates for memories” switch in source/privacy details. Explain that prior discarded dates cannot be recovered and location metadata stays discarded.
decisions.reason: This is a privacy-sensitive tradeoff with a meaningful benefit. Do not silently enable it for prettier memories.

controls.label: Keep only the capture date from new imports

decisions.title: Approve / Reject selected
decisions.alternative: Inside the pending-photo queue, show actions only after selection. Reject explains whether the picture is excluded persistently; empty queue shows completion without commands.
decisions.reason: Approval is a task with prerequisites. Always-visible actions on an empty queue create confusing furniture.

decisions.title: Import photos / muted clip
decisions.alternative: A single Add action in the library opens Photos or Muted clip, followed by Android’s picker. Show concise duration/size limits, progress, result and actionable failure.
decisions.reason: Importing is content creation. Separate permanent buttons and codec prose do not belong on the default Settings page.

decisions.title: Choose / remove soundtrack
decisions.alternative: No file: Add soundtrack. File present: show a safe display name, Replace and contextual Remove. Use a native picker and make the supported formats discoverable in help.
decisions.reason: State determines which operations make sense. Do not show Remove before a soundtrack exists.

decisions.title: Play soundtrack / volume
decisions.alternative: Only with a soundtrack present, show an Audio switch and themed volume slider with audible preview on explicit request. Stop audio on cancel/exit; preserve mute defaults.
decisions.reason: Volume is genuinely continuous, so a slider is appropriate. Audio should never start as a surprise from opening Settings.

decisions.title: Automatic photos only during these hours
decisions.alternative: In Frame → Daily routine, show automatic photos enabled/disabled and their active window. Reveal times only when scheduling is enabled.
decisions.reason: This governs the whole frame. Displaying inactive times makes disabled behavior look configured and active.

controls.label: Automatic photos only during these hours

decisions.title: Photo schedule From / Until
decisions.alternative: Two labeled time pickers in the chosen clock format, with an overnight-aware summary and the selected city’s time shown.
decisions.reason: Times justify time controls. Describe the range in natural language so crossing midnight is understandable.

decisions.title: Set app brightness by schedule
decisions.alternative: A brightness schedule row explains that only Skylit’s window is affected. Enable reveals day/night brightness and the actual effective window.
decisions.reason: A behavior affecting the whole display should not be hidden among photo editing tools.

decisions.title: Scheduled / outside brightness
decisions.alternative: Themed sliders labeled for their effective periods, with brightness icons and visible values. Preview temporarily; restore normal system behavior when disabled.
decisions.reason: Brightness is a continuous perceptual choice. A slider fits, but generic blue bars without clear state and feedback do not.

decisions.title: Save slideshow as / Save preset
decisions.alternative: Save as presentation opens a name sheet with a thumbnail summary, Save and Cancel. It does not expose an empty name box continuously.
decisions.reason: This creates an object. Object creation deserves a small focused flow.

decisions.title: Saved presets / Load / Delete
decisions.alternative: Named cards show collection/style. Open to preview and Use; contextual menu contains Rename/Delete. Show empty state rather than an empty dropdown.
decisions.reason: Load/delete commands around a blank select expose file-management mechanics rather than a recognizable collection of presentations.

decisions.title: Seasonal / From month / Through month
decisions.alternative: An “Use during these months” switch within one presentation’s details reveals named month pickers. Show a natural range including year-wrap behavior.
decisions.reason: Month numbers are an internal encoding. The range belongs to a particular presentation, not a general photo form.

decisions.title: Title cards, title and closing title
decisions.alternative: Default has no title cards. An Add title action opens an optional title/closing-title editor with immediate visual preview and a clear Remove title route.
decisions.reason: This is deliberate presentation authoring. It must not reintroduce captions or persistent controls on the slideshow player.

decisions.title: Seconds per title / exported slide
decisions.alternative: Export follows the presentation’s pace by default. A timing row allows deliberate overrides through human duration choices and shows estimated total length.
decisions.reason: Two raw numbers do not explain the resulting movie. Some timing choices are valid; their consequences should be visible.

decisions.title: Export video / Cancel export
decisions.alternative: Export from the selected presentation or selected photos, with a summary and native destination flow. Cancel appears only while work runs; completion opens/shares the actual output.
decisions.reason: Export has prerequisites, progress and an artifact. It should not be a standing preference button with unrelated timing fields.

decisions.title: Start / Stop phone session
decisions.alternative: Inactive: Manage from phone. Active flow: QR, matching number, frame approval, expiry and Stop. Show verification help at the relevant certificate step.
decisions.reason: Start and Stop are opposite states, not permanent peer commands. Keep normal expiry, immediate revocation and local-only scope.

decisions.title: Show photos after
decisions.alternative: Automatic photos on/off, then visible 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 minute delay choices when enabled. Show a short “after no touch” explanation.
decisions.reason: Never and durations mix enablement with a parameter. Make both concepts explicit without showing inactive parameters.

decisions.title: Shared album link / Save album
decisions.alternative: Only for the shared-album source, a focused private-link entry with Connect/Cancel and meaningful validation. Show saved status without displaying the secret link.
decisions.reason: A credential-like URL genuinely needs input, but should not sit below unrelated local-library tools.

decisions.title: Preview idle photo mode
decisions.alternative: In Daily routine, “Try automatic display” demonstrates the chosen source and return behavior, then returns to the same setting.
decisions.reason: Previewing automatic display is valid. Its label must distinguish it from previewing a manual slideshow.

decisions.title: Quiet ambient display
decisions.alternative: “Quiet display at night” with a visual example of the clock-only state. Times appear only when enabled; scope explains that active manual playback is not interrupted.
decisions.reason: This is a whole-frame privacy behavior, not a photo setting. Demonstration makes the policy understandable.

controls.label: Quiet ambient display during these hours

decisions.title: Quiet From / Until
decisions.alternative: Use the same readable time-range interaction as other routines. Show any intentional difference from photo/brightness hours and permit it explicitly.
decisions.reason: Consolidation should reveal relationships without forcing saved independent schedules to match.

decisions.title: Pause private content now
decisions.alternative: An easily reached Pause action in Frame and a suitable quick-action route. While paused show Resume and current scope; do not bury it below the photo tool suite.
decisions.reason: An immediate privacy operation must be reachable at the moment it is needed, not found by searching long preference forms.

decisions.title: Review who appears
decisions.alternative: Event visibility row shows Off, On or pending count. Open a nested review tool; highlight only real pending work.
decisions.reason: It is neither a calendar account field nor a global top-level setting. State should precede an empty queue.

controls.label: Review who appears on this frame

decisions.title: Show on frame
decisions.alternative: One labeled switch in each connected-calendar row, with immediate dashboard/calendar effect and reversible state.
decisions.reason: This is a genuine entity-specific binary preference. Keep it adjacent to the calendar label.

decisions.title: Edit / Remove calendar
decisions.alternative: Tap the calendar row to open details. Rename/color there; Remove in its contextual menu with scope and confirmation.
decisions.reason: Repeated equal-weight editing commands clutter the connected list. Removal is a deliberate source operation.

decisions.title: Calendar name
decisions.alternative: A labeled name field in Add/Edit calendar, with a meaningful default only when safely available and a clear cancel route.
decisions.reason: Naming an entity requires text; changing its location does not justify replacing it with a visual-only control.

decisions.title: Calendar colour
decisions.alternative: Five color swatches with names and a selection marker, beside the label preview. Never rely solely on color to identify a calendar.
decisions.reason: Appearance is visual. A text dropdown hides the effect and asks people to translate a color name.

decisions.title: Secret iCal address / Connect
decisions.alternative: A masked private-feed entry with on-device help, Connect/Cancel and real refresh verification. Keep stored links hidden after saving.
decisions.reason: The necessary form should be carefully designed, not abolished. Retain read-only private-feed integration and existing privacy boundaries.

decisions.title: Review new inviters
decisions.alternative: Event visibility starts with “Review new event organizers” on/off. Disabled state hides queues and policy details; enabling explains scope before setup.
decisions.reason: Do not bury enablement inside setup while showing a disabled feature as an empty active workflow.

controls.label: Review new inviters before showing their events

decisions.title: Calendar account email
decisions.alternative: A focused owner-identity field inside review setup, explaining its role; keep the actual value private and editable on-device.
decisions.reason: This is legitimate exact-address information, but not an everyday control above every review decision.

decisions.title: Approve inviter / Approve action
decisions.alternative: Pending items present exact addresses with Show/Hide decisions. A separate Add approved person sheet takes a typed address and explicit confirmation.
decisions.reason: Normal review should use known pending entities; manual entry is a distinct exceptional task.

decisions.title: Show events without organizer
decisions.alternative: A clear “Show events with no organizer” switch in review policy, with an example of what that means.
decisions.reason: It is a meaningful fallback policy, but belongs beside review configuration rather than as a global always-visible choice.

controls.label: Show events without an organizer address

decisions.title: Show Household
decisions.alternative: Dashboard → Visible pages has a single Household switch with an example of the navigation item.
decisions.reason: Optional-page visibility currently has three scattered homes.

decisions.title: Open Household
decisions.alternative: A concise Manage notes & lists link from relevant context. Widget edit links open the same activity even if its navigation entry is hidden.
decisions.reason: An activity launch is useful; it should replace the embedded content form, not duplicate it.

decisions.title: Pinned note / Save note
decisions.alternative: Edit the note in Household or from its widget, with a focused textarea and Save/Cancel. Show the intended widget preview, not an unrelated preference card.
decisions.reason: Text entry is appropriate; the problem is context and draft semantics, not the existence of a form.

decisions.title: Countdown title / date / Add
decisions.alternative: Add countdown in Household or widget context opens title/date fields and a resulting countdown preview, with Add/Cancel.
decisions.reason: These are creation fields for an object. They should not remain blank on a settings page.

decisions.title: Google Home page / Save
decisions.alternative: Use the supported default entry. Open Google Home and sign in on the frame. If custom destinations serve a verified need, edit through a labeled connection-detail flow with exact host restrictions.
decisions.reason: Raw URL configuration is not the normal goal. A destination loaded successfully still does not prove home control.

decisions.title: Show Home / Show YouTube
decisions.alternative: Place the two switches beside Household under Dashboard → Visible pages; demonstrate the navigation result.
decisions.reason: One conceptual preference family should have one home and one consistent interaction.

decisions.title: Shortcut title / link / Add
decisions.alternative: Create a shortcut in YouTube, with a link field, validated recognizable type, optional title and Add/Cancel. Edit existing shortcuts through their own menus.
decisions.reason: A content-making workflow should be tied to its output; necessary link entry stays, but the empty standing form goes.

decisions.title: Main update action / Check now
decisions.alternative: One primary action follows actual state: Check, Download or Install. A secondary Check again is offered when relevant, not as a competing duplicate.
decisions.reason: State dictates the next step. Automatic policy does not remove an owner’s ability to act manually.

decisions.title: Allow install permission
decisions.alternative: Explain why Android permission is needed and open its settings only when the owner chooses install/idle updates. Resume the update flow afterward.
decisions.reason: Permission is a prerequisite step, not ordinary permanent preference furniture. Keep denial and unsupported states clear.

decisions.title: Automatic check/download/install
decisions.alternative: Manual / Check automatically / Download automatically / Update while idle, with a short consequence for each. Preserve current combinations as an explicit equivalent or Custom state until the owner chooses.
decisions.reason: Three independent flags expose a pipeline. An owner-facing policy avoids invalid or surprising combinations without silently enabling automation.

controls.label: Install automatically while the frame is idle

decisions.title: Update window
decisions.alternative: Only for idle installation, offer natural time pickers in the chosen format and a readable overnight summary. State Android confirmation requirements where applicable.
decisions.reason: A 24-entry hour dropdown is a poor time picker. The window is irrelevant when automatic installation is off.

decisions.title: Wi-Fi / wireless / Android apps
decisions.alternative: Frame → Android & connections offers labeled icon rows. Show recovery guidance beside wireless settings and return cleanly to Skylit.
decisions.reason: These solve a real owner need. They deserve approachable labels and clear effects, rather than three equal technical buttons.

decisions.title: Weather/Calendar Retry; mail Check now; Home Open
decisions.alternative: Healthy fetch services use Refresh; failed services use Retry with reason. Mail uses Check now; Home uses Open with verified-capability state. Only relevant actions appear.
decisions.reason: Generic Retry in a healthy row is misleading. Keep the distinction between rendering a remote page and verified service function.

decisions.title: Repeated service Settings buttons
decisions.alternative: A service row opens the canonical connection page, with a clear return to status. Avoid a repeated button beside every row when the row itself is the route.
decisions.reason: Repeated labels consume attention and can create multiple configuration homes.

decisions.title: Open setup guide
decisions.alternative: Help offers the guide; incomplete or failed service rows link to the relevant step. Reopening does not reset settings or expose credentials.
decisions.reason: Help is valuable when connected to a problem. It should not be buried between diagnostic and transfer forms.

decisions.title: Open original Skylight app
decisions.alternative: Keep a clearly named fallback under Android apps/recovery, with a reliable return route.
decisions.reason: The original launcher/app is a recovery resource, not an everyday appearance preference.

decisions.title: Export preferences
decisions.alternative: Export a preferences file through the Android file/share flow, showing a compact scope summary and result. Keep private credentials/content excluded.
decisions.reason: Export produces an artifact and needs destination/result feedback, not raw serialized text.

decisions.title: Import file
decisions.alternative: Choose a file, validate it, preview supported changes and omissions, then Apply/Cancel. Preserve unrelated settings and explain failures specifically.
decisions.reason: This is the appropriate form of data transfer. Do not imply that unsupported dashboard layouts or private content will be restored.

decisions.title: JSON textarea / Import pasted
decisions.alternative: Remove pasted JSON from normal Settings. Use the native file flow; any debugging representation belongs in developer tools outside the owner interface.
decisions.reason: This exposes the storage format and requires technical literacy without improving the household task.
